description:
Redwood Inference’s Optimize product can apply cost-saving configuration changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles) that materially affect model outputs. This project, “Quality guardrails gating for optimize,” adds mandatory quality evaluation checks and regression thresholds before any Optimize recommendation can be applied (automatically or via one-click) to production traffic.

Goals:
- Prevent silent quality regressions caused by cost optimizations (e.g., more aggressive batching, cache changes, or quantization profile switches).
- Define consistent, measurable quality gates (offline evals + online canary signals) with clear pass/fail criteria.
- Provide a traceable approval/audit trail: what changed, why it was suggested, which evals ran, and who approved/overrode.
- Keep developer experience fast: make “safe-by-default” the path while allowing documented exceptions.

Scope (in-scope):
- Config change types: batching policy updates, prefix/KV caching settings, and quantization profile changes (per model family/hardware SKU).
- Gating pipeline: trigger eval runs on proposed config diffs; compute quality deltas vs baseline; enforce thresholds; surface results in Console/Optimize.
- Rollout integration: require gates before enabling a canary rollout; block full rollout on failures; auto-rollback hooks.
- Observability: dashboards/alerts for gate failures, flaky evals, and drift; logging of gate decisions.

Out of scope (initially):
- Full private/on-prem automation (will be designed but delivered later); manual workflow + documentation first.
- New model onboarding process overhaul (only integrate with existing eval harness and prompt sets).

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Product: Aditya Rao (Optimize) owns PRD and launch; Paula Mendes (Rollouts/telemetry) owns rollout coupling.
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Karthik Iyer, Selene Huang own gate metrics, eval methodology, and prompt-set coverage.
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez / Noah Patel / Sofia Ivanova ensure config diffs map cleanly to runtime behavior and have safe fallbacks.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant define SLO impact signals, dashboards, and alerting; Connor O’Brien + Sahana Iyer support CI integration.

Phases & timeline (plausible):
- Discovery + requirements (2025-10 to 2025-11): define gate metrics, thresholds, supported config types, and exception policy.
- Design (2025-11 to 2025-12): architecture, data model (gate runs, baselines), integration points (Optimize service, eval-harness, Console), and rollout coupling.
- Implementation + internal beta (2026-01): gating enforced in staging + select internal workloads; fix flakiness and runtime edge cases.
- Limited production rollout (2026-02): enforce gates for Optimize changes in hosted API for a subset of routes/accounts.
- GA + expansion (2026-03+): extend to Dedicated defaults and broader model families; private workflow support.

Constraints / non-functional requirements:
- Eval runtime and cost must be bounded (tiered gates: fast smoke gates vs full gates).
- Statistical rigor: handle variance; require minimum sample sizes; track and mitigate flaky prompt sets.
- Backwards compatibility: existing manual config changes must be supported but logged and (where possible) gated.
- Clear override mechanics: time-bound exceptions with explicit owners and follow-ups.
